lead: Accountability and evidence dominate the overnight batch: a routing layer answers the canary investigation, the full Ghostscript research article keeps its tested scope, and UN talks on autonomous weapons fail under their own consensus rule. A prize essay on conscious AI, a hypothetical Riemann discussion and a legal-data service each argue more than they prove.
A link post, a marketing-ready anxiety and a vendor coverage register round out the day: personal accounts and self-published figures are recorded with their limits attached.

The late-morning batch adds a provider's own canary-incident disclosure, modeled emissions for one lab's buildout and excerpt-only chip-espionage reporting, plus an investor's cyber-risk thesis and a driver-assistance visualization whose claims remain marketing.

The afternoon adds a game about delegated work and a physics-coding comparison, alongside arguments about emissions, wealth and supply-chain dependence. Limited-access industrial-security and taste reporting keep their evidentiary boundaries.

The late batch adds a proposed loss-based pacing standard, local-serving and safety-course resources, and a claimed mathematical advance whose acceptance is not established. Outage explanations and hiring anecdotes keep their different evidence levels.

sections.title: A routing layer answers the canary investigation
sections.intro: OpenRouter's incident announcement responds to the Dragos findings without claiming a new experiment or a breach of its own systems.

sections.title: The full renderer research keeps its tested scope
sections.intro: The Upload2Shell article behind yesterday's disclosure index separates demonstrated delegate chains from paths only traced to the renderer.

sections.title: Consensus blocks an autonomous-weapons mandate
sections.intro: A week of UN talks ends with a weaker instrument after objections attributed to Russia and reluctance from several military powers.

sections.title: A prize essay argues, and a hypothetical explores
sections.intro: Anil Seth's case against conscious AI and a panel's thought experiment about a machine proof are positions and speculation, not results.

sections.title: A legal corpus publishes what it does not hold
sections.intro: Pandex pairs its European law API and MCP server with an unusually explicit register of coverage gaps, all self-reported.

sections.title: A link post endorses a process, not a product
sections.intro: Simon Willison points to Graham Dumpleton's documented AI-assisted build of the Muru server without claiming a tested evaluation.

sections.title: Espionage anxiety is marketing-ready before it is measured
sections.intro: Wired collects matchmaker anecdotes about honeypot fears while one matchmaker reports no increase and vendors already sell reassurance.

sections.title: A provider incident confirms the canary findings
sections.intro: Together AI's own disclosure shows the Dragos canary credentials were downloaded from its stored prompt samples, in the provider's words.

sections.title: Chip acquisition reporting arrives as excerpts
sections.intro: Two blocked primaries describe a state campaign and a smuggling case; both remain attributed reporting that could not be read in full.

sections.title: The buildout's costs are modeled and renegotiated
sections.intro: A research group models Anthropic's fossil-heavy power mix while suppliers reportedly reopen signed server contracts for higher prices.

sections.title: One loop, every device
sections.intro: A hobby compiler project promises CPU-to-multi-GPU execution without a GPU toolkit, on its own measurements.

sections.title: An investor prices a cyber epidemic
sections.intro: Bridgewater's one-in-three estimate is a portfolio judgment built on its own incident pipeline, not a consensus measurement.

sections.title: A rendering is not the road
sections.intro: Tesla's v15 pairs a photorealistic visualization with marketing safety multiples that remain unverified.

sections.title: A game and a spring toy test what approval hides
sections.intro: A role-reversal game exposes the gap between reports and task completion; an anecdotal simulation comparison exposes the gap between plausible motion and the requested physics.

sections.title: Climate estimates meet wealth and supply-chain arguments
sections.intro: A climate newsletter combines studies with different boundaries, an investor describes paper wealth, and an export-control commentary argues causation without isolating it.

sections.title: Limited access constrains two broader claims
sections.intro: The FT feed describes faster industrial-attack preparation, while an accessible NYT opening debates taste. Neither establishes the larger capability claim suggested by its theme.

sections.title: A proposed pacing metric needs a shared denominator
sections.intro: OpenAI discloses its internal prediction-loss series while explaining why neither the dataset nor a capability forecast is yet a cross-lab safety standard.

sections.title: Local serving and a safety syllabus make their boundaries visible
sections.intro: A home-hosting guide separates model memory from context, while a graduate course page maps safety questions without turning lecture topics into research results.

sections.title: Hiring signals and a claimed proof resist broad conclusions
sections.intro: One employer reports a screening problem; a commentator interprets a reported mathematical claim. Neither supplies a general causal test or independent proof verification.

sections.title: Upgrades, adviser controls and a missing opinion text
sections.intro: Reported explanations distinguish outages from attacks, IPO controls remain source-attributed, and an inaccessible opinion is recorded without inventing its argument.
